A grading system, as determined by the British Association of
Otolaryngologists, Head and Neck Surgeons, is also used for the
- Very mild (score 0–16). Tinnitus is perceived only in silence and is
easily masked. It does not interfere with sleep or with daily activities.
- Mild (score 18–36). Tinnitus is easily masked by environmental
sounds and forgotten during daily activities. It can occasionally
interfere with sleep but not with daily activities.
- Moderate (score 38–56). Tinnitus is perceived even in the
presence of environmental sound; however, daily activities are not
impaired. It is perceived less under concentration. Interference with
sleep and relaxing activities is not infrequent.
- Severe (score 58–76). Tinnitus is continuously perceived and
hardly masked by external noise. It alters the sleep cycle and can
interfere with the subject’s daily activities. Relaxing activities are
compromised. Subjects with this level of tinnitus often require
- Catastrophic (78–90). All side effects caused by tinnitus are
present at a very severe level. The subject requires medical
assistance very frequently, including neuropsychiatric help.
A  change  score  of  at  least  seven  points  has  been  considered
to denote reliable clinically significant improvement on the THI
